currentTitleDe: Energetische Kopplung endergoner und exergoner Reaktionen erklären
currentTitleEn: Explain energetic coupling of endergonic and exergonic reactions
currentDescriptionDe: Die lernende Person kann die energetische Kopplung einer endergonen mit einer exergonen Reaktion erklären und auftretende Energieunterschiede als Entropieerzeugung interpretieren.
currentDescriptionEn: The learner can explain the energetic coupling of an endergonic reaction with an exergonic reaction and interpret occurring energy differences as entropy production.

understandingEvidence.essentialUnderstandingDe: Kopplung benötigt einen gemeinsamen chemischen Weg, etwa ein aktiviertes Zwischenprodukt oder einen Enzymtransfer. Die vollständige Gibbs-Bilanz kann günstig sein; bei begrenzten T,p- und Arbeitsbedingungen wird ihr Rest als T mal Entropieerzeugung bilanziert.
understandingEvidence.essentialUnderstandingEn: Coupling requires a shared chemical pathway such as an activated intermediate or enzyme transfer. The complete Gibbs balance can be favourable; under bounded T,p and work conditions its remainder is accounted for as T times entropy generation.
understandingEvidence.observablePerformanceDe: Die Person bilanziert +15 und -30 kJ/mol zu -15 kJ/mol, zeigt den gemeinsamen AP-Weg und den ausgeglichenen Gesamtumsatz; bei 300 K und ohne zusätzliche Nutzarbeit begründet sie 50 J/(mol K) Entropieerzeugung.
understandingEvidence.observablePerformanceEn: The learner sums +15 and -30 kJ/mol to -15 kJ/mol, identifies the shared AP route and balanced net reaction, and explains 50 J/(mol K) entropy generation at 300 K without extra useful work.
understandingEvidence.transferExpectationDe: Am Hexokinase-Fall begründet sie den direkten Phosphattransfer aus ATP auf Glucose; getrennte ATP-Hydrolyse in einem anderen Gefäß koppelt die endergone Reaktion nicht chemisch.
understandingEvidence.transferExpectationEn: In the hexokinase case, the learner explains direct phosphate transfer from ATP to glucose; separate ATP hydrolysis in another vessel does not chemically couple the endergonic reaction.

rationale: Fresh current coupling image/native review after the original eleven and5169 successor were sealed. The exact corrected PNG uses abstract interlocking puzzle pieces to show a shared reaction pathway, valid ΔG1<0/ΔG2>0 and a favourable total ΔG. It correctly shows -ΔGtotal=T*Sgen with Sgen>0, constant T,p and no further useful work; the labels remain readable at original/360/680 sizes. It neither adds entropy to energy nor labels entropy as heat. The complete closed single-reservoir model used for this relation is bounded by the whole matching P cases; it is not a universal open-cell balance. The actual complete PDF page has unchanged equivalent DE/EN goal semantics and full prerequisite/context links without clipping. Both complete cases, material/data, model answers and rubrics were reread, including shared A-P formation and direct enzyme phosphate transfer rather than unrelated ATP hydrolysis. No molecular mass claim is made by the puzzle icon. The original hold is resolved for this exact pending-QA successor only; later QA/page changes require new bindings. No learner/lab execution or human approval is asserted.
